ResearchProjectDef.label: functional flowers
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Functional flowers are the other half of the garden: they turn mana into labour instead of making it. A generating flower feeds the pool; a functional flower only spends what the pool already holds, converting material, mending gear, quieting a mind or holding ground, and never puts a single point of mana back.

What they share is a bill and a leash. Each one prices its work in mana and settles on a fixed timer, and each only works while its own tile sits inside a mana network: coverage = 4 tiles from a simple pool, 7 from a manasteel pool, 11 from a relay, and a relay only counts when its circle overlaps a pool-backed group. Outside every circle there is nothing to draw on; inside one the flower pays its printed price out of the group's shared reserve, and a full manasteel pool holds 100,000 mana to pay with. A flower that cannot pay skips that action; whether it has a fallback is stated on its own project. Bottom line: no pool, no work.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: pure daisy
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A white daisy that teaches dead material to live. One log becomes one livingwood, and one cut stone block (granite, limestone and the like, not raw chunks) becomes one livingrock. It reaches only the eight tiles around itself, and only items lying loose on the ground: anything forbidden or packed inside a container is left alone.

On a paying pool (a mana pool within 6 tiles) it converts one item every 300 ticks, 5 seconds, for 20 mana. With no pool in reach, or a pool holding less than 20 mana, it still converts, but once every 1,500 ticks, 25 seconds, and for free. Bottom line: 20 mana ÷ 5 s = 4 mana per second with a pool; the same item takes 25 s and 0 mana without one, so a lone daisy bootstraps livingwood at a fifth of the speed.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: clear-mind lotus
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A pale lotus that pushes one thought out of every head within 8 tiles. It only cancels the psychic drone: with a psychic droner building on the map the drone thought is switched off outright, and for an event drone with no building the mood penalty is only halved. No drone, no bill, and no other mood is touched.

It charges per protected head every 60 ticks (one second): 20 mana for each pawn the drone is actually affecting, nothing for pawns the drone ignores. One payment holds for 180 ticks (3 seconds). It never pays half a bill: if the network cannot cover the whole cost the pawns are handed to another lotus, and the drone returns once the last paid window lapses. Bottom line: 20 mana per affected pawn per second, so 5 pawns × 20 = 100 mana per second.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: thorn flower
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A mat of briars with a dark bloom at its heart. Every 90 ticks (1.5 seconds) it looks 10 tiles around and entangles every hostile pawn in reach for 90 ticks, moving at 70% speed; that slow is free and costs no mana at all.

The thorns themselves are paid per target: up to 12 hostiles per pulse, 1 cut damage and 2 mana each, nearest first. It carries a 150-mana buffer fed by the network, so a full buffer pays for 75 hits, and with no hostile in range it refills by up to 25 mana per pulse, about 17 per second. Bottom line: 12 targets × 2 mana = 24 mana per pulse (12 damage), 16 mana per second sustained; with no mana left the briars still slow but deal nothing.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: mana mending
ResearchProjectDef.description:
Not a flower but the rule behind two repair devices: a tower that mends built structures and a bench that mends worn gear. Both settle once every 60 ticks (one second), take the most damaged valid targets first, and pay 5 mana for every point of hit points they put back.

The bill scales with the work: 5 hp costs 25 mana, and a device restoring 5 hp per second on each of five targets draws 125 mana per second. If the network covers only part of the bill the device repairs only what it can pay for, and with no mana it does nothing that second. Bottom line: hp restored × 5 mana = the bill, settled every 60 ticks; no free repairs, and neither device can finish construction or mend a blueprint or frame.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: structure repairer
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A livingrock frame with a wall of mana-veined stone. Every 60 ticks (one second) it scans 8 tiles for your own structures below full hit points, skips blueprints, frames and corpses, and takes the five most damaged by default.

Each target gets up to 5 hp back per cycle at 5 mana per hp, so a full patch costs 25 mana; five targets at full stretch draw 125 mana per second. It only repairs what the network can pay for, and with no mana it stops. Bottom line: 5 hp × 5 mana = 25 mana per target per second, 8-tile reach, five targets by default. It will not finish construction and will not touch another faction's walls.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.

ResearchProjectDef.label: item repairer
ResearchProjectDef.description:
A livingwood bench with a manasteel anvil and a clamp of woven mana. Every 60 ticks (one second) it scans 6 tiles for items with hit points that are below full condition, ignores pawns, plants, corpses, blueprints and frames, and takes the five most damaged by default.

Each item gets up to 6 hp back per cycle at 5 mana per hp, so a full patch costs 30 mana; five items at full stretch draw 150 mana per second. It only repairs what the network can pay for. Bottom line: 6 hp × 5 mana = 30 mana per target per second, 6-tile reach, five targets by default. Gear has to lie on the ground, and something already destroyed cannot be restored.

Full numbers and derivations: gameplay guide.
